purpose of this study is to increase the accuracy of the physical parameters of a solar cell in the electron̶ hole production rate
equation. In previous studies, this section was neglected because of using only ready-made software. Simulations were performed
using a one-dimensional difusion model in MATLAB and Maple software. Ten, in theory, we simulated cadmium telluride-
based layered solar cells for the frst time without using ready-made software and with coding in MATLAB and Maple software.
We designed and optimized the thickness of the layers in solar cells in detail. Ten we studied the efect of layer thickness on the
short-circuit current (Jsc), open-circuit voltage (Voc), flling factor (FF), and its efciency. It is found that the efciency of solar
cells layered with TCO/SnO2/CdS/CdTe layers is as follows: the thickness of the TCO layer is 0.1 μm, that of the SnO2 layer is equal
to 0.1 μm, that of the CdS layer as the window layer is 0.1 μm and the thickness of the CdTe layer as the absorber layer is 3.9 μm. Te
efciency of the solar cell with the TCO/SnO2/CdS/CdTe structure increases signifcantly and reaches a maximum value of more
than 20%.

in numerical calculations are not visible. Results are pre-

work from other studies that have been done so far is
avoiding the use of ready-made simulation software. Because
optimization requires a proper understanding of physical
processes, we frst coded in MATLAB and Maple software.

performance of a multilayer solar cell by calculating un-
restricted parameters in terms of independent and limited
variables. Layers and their impact on open-circuit voltage,
short-circuit current, flling factor, and efciency have been
carefully studied [26].

model, adding a layer for optical trapping and thus com-
pensating for the reduction of current, and fnally engi-
